Istanbul air and traffic dashboard

Open data of the municipality (air-quality stations, traffic index) with weather and a model: the published AQI reconstructed and checked, the daily rhythm, weather-normalised trends, traffic and its holidays, the lockdowns as a natural experiment and city-wide episodes. Every number on this page is computed from the data snapshot.

The air-quality index, reconstructed

The municipality publishes an AQI next to the concentrations. Fitting its numbers shows how it is made: the US EPA scale with breakpoints converted to µg/m³; PM10 averaged over 24 h, O₃ and CO over 8 h, SO₂ and NO₂ hourly (at least half of the window valid); the overall index is the largest sub-index. Fitting the breakpoints on half of the stations reproduces the other half.

A run of identical values counts as stuck when it would occur by chance less than 0.5 times in the series (from the series’ own repeat probability). Both rules are validated on planted faults (README, `sehir dogrulama`).

Daily and weekly rhythm

NO₂ follows the rush hours, O₃ the afternoon sun; on weekends traffic-related NO₂ is lower and O₃ is not.

Ratios come from paired weeks (log of the weekend mean minus log of the weekday mean, Student-t interval); O₃ at or above 1 on weekends is the known “weekend effect”: less NO fresh from traffic means less ozone is consumed.

Weather and trends

Wind and a shallow boundary layer decide how much of what is emitted stays near the station. Daily log-concentration models of weather, calendar and a time trend explain cross-validated R² of 0.33 (NO₂) and 0.48 (PM10) in the median (each year predicted from the others).

Traffic

The traffic index is the municipality’s congestion index (0 free-flowing … 100 gridlock), not a vehicle count.

What the calendar and the weather do

Public holidays on weekdays: -41 % [-47, -35] against the same weekday in the weeks around (46 holidays). Rainy days (≥ 1 mm): +7.5 % [+5.1, +10.0] after weekday, month and holidays (511 rainy days).

Two independent sources agree: the daily means of the hourly feed and the published daily file correlate at r = 0.978 over 1067 days (means 30.2 and 30.6).

A check against what the government announced. The nine-day bayram holidays of 2024 added the weekdays 8–9 April and 20–21 June; the detector, which only knows weekdays, months and the public-holiday list, flagged 4 of 4 of them (2024-04-08, 2024-04-09, 2024-06-20, 2024-06-21). It also flags the days before bayrams, election Sundays (14 and 28 May 2023, 31 March 2024) and New Year’s Eve.

The lockdowns as a natural experiment

In spring 2020 and from 29 April to 17 May 2021 Istanbul traffic collapsed. Each station’s daily log-concentration is modelled from weather, calendar and a time trend on all days outside the windows; the mean residual inside a window is ranked among the mean residuals of all other windows of the same length.

windowtraffic index, 4 weeks beforein the windowchange
2020 spring27.110.5-61 %
2021 full lockdown23.59.8-58 %

Across the stations

pollutantwindowstationsmedian changestations with a decreasesign test p
NO22020 spring11-18 %9 of 110.065
NO22021 full lockdown10-26 %8 of 100.11
PM102020 spring8+1 %4 of 81.00
PM102021 full lockdown13-25 %10 of 130.092
The strongest single result is NO₂ at Aksaray in 2021 (-63 %, z = -6.5 against the placebo windows). Across stations NO₂ fell at 8 of 10 in 2021 (sign test p 0.11), so the sign is consistent but not conclusive at 5 %; PM10 fell as well in 2021, so weather the model does not see may play a part. Treat the picture as supportive, not as a measured emissions effect.

Episodes and the model

When the median PM10 of the stations is at or above 50 µg/m³ the whole city is affected, not one street: the first principal component carries 69 % of the variance of the stations’ daily PM10 (against 54 % for NO₂). During episodes the wind blew from the SE (154°) far more often than by chance (Rayleigh p < 0.001, 403 days).

The CAMS model’s dust field, which knows nothing about the stations, is a regional signal that agrees with them: on 53 % of the days when dust is high (top 5 %) the stations are in an episode (odds ratio 8.1, Fisher p < 0.001). Only 20 % of the episode days have high modelled dust, so most episodes are not dust.

CAMS against the stations

Median over stations: NO₂ normalised bias -32 %, r = 0.62; PM10 bias -12 %, r = 0.65. A 10 km model cannot see street canyons: it underestimates NO₂ most at the traffic stations (Aksaray, D-100).

Data snapshot of 2026-10-13: hourly air quality of 13 stations from 2019-01-01, traffic index hourly since 2021-11-08 and daily 2015-08-06 – 2024-10-18, ERA5 weather and CAMS model for central Istanbul.
